source.question: An ideal 9 V source drives a 3 ohm resistor in series with a pair of 6 ohm resistors in parallel. Determine the source current, the voltage across the parallel pair and both branch currents. Explain whether each branch sees the full 9 V.

initial_model_options.label: A series resistor feeds a two-node parallel pair
All three resistors are directly across the source

task.prediction: Will the measured source current constrain a hidden positive resistor to a unique value?
task.stem: An ideal 18 V source drives a 3 ohm resistor in series with two parallel branches. One branch contains 6 ohm; the other contains a finite, positive unknown resistance R. An ideal ammeter before the junction reads 4 A. Find R, the two-node branch voltage and both branch currents. Verify charge and voltage balance. A student says each branch receives 18 V; evaluate that claim.

model_options.label: 3 ohm in series with a parallel two-node block
All three resistors directly across 18 V
Both branch currents must be equal

boundary.stem: For the same ideal 18 V source with fixed 3 ohm series element and fixed 6 ohm parallel branch, classify measurements of 7 A and 1.5 A when only finite positive R changes. Provide both current limits, and explain how open-branch and short-branch limits differ from finite positive R.

conditions: Ideal 18 V supply; constant ohmic positive resistances; 3 ohm series before two-node parallel block; no wire short or hidden extra load.
All educational prompts are original authored candidate tasks, not validated past-paper Core2 material.
